doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Dr. Carroll, the history teacher
summary: Johnson and Baker remember Dr. Carroll as an intense, brilliant, humorless teacher of black history.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Was Dr. Carroll your history teacher? Was he there, because I remember . . .
Dr. Carroll was one of my teachers at one time, and it must have been history, right? Because that was his bag.
One of the first people to teach black history.
He was very intense – a brilliant, brilliant man, but very intense, and a hard – he ran a tight ship.
He ran a tight ship, a very tight ship. He was a very severe, serious person with no sense of humor whatsoever, [laughs], but a brilliant man.
